QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_42

question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about funds settlement timing for ETIRD?

answer.text: Funds settlement through clearing banks happens before market hours on the settlement day
Funds settle in real-time during market hours
Funds settle at the end of the trading day after market close
Funds settle within one hour of the trade execution

explanation.text: The Logic: Funds settlement through clearing banks occurs before market hours on the settlement day (T+1). This ensures that all obligations are met before the next trading session begins. The Trap: Real-time settlement is not the process for exchange-traded derivatives. End of day and one-hour settlements are incorrect. The pre-market timing ensures clean opening of next day's trading. Cross-Exam Context: Settlement timing rules are consistent across derivative segments. Understanding the pre-market settlement window is important for operational compliance. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Clearing banks have specific cutoff times (typically early morning) for pay-in. Treasury teams must plan overnight funding to meet these deadlines.
